subject: ENG
course_description: Readings in the medieval and subsequent Arthurian tradition.
course_notes: The historical King Arthur probably had a Roman father and a Celtic mother. As King of the Britons he combated the Angles and the Saxons, the very people who became the English and who claimed¿without irony--their former adversary as a national hero. The Britons, the English, and the French then created the corpus of Arthurian legend that continues to grow today. We will read a range of medieval and modern texts in order to understand how the legend--known as the Matter of Britain--defines the mythic imagination and how the legend explores fate and free will, heroic conduct, the supernatural, courtly love, chivalry, and the origin of evil. This course fulfills the pre-1700 requirement for the English major. Texts: Latin chronicles; Middle English Breton Lays; Sir Gawain and the Green Knight; Sir Thomas Malory, Morte Darthur; Mark Twain, A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur¿s Court; C. S. Lewis, That Hideous Strength; Kazuo Ishiguro, The Buried Giant.
